features.description: Fix the OTLP/JSON trace/span ID decode defect at all three receiver sites, TEST-FIRST. internal/observatory/otlp_receiver.go:166 decodes with protojson.Unmarshal, which follows the proto3 JSON mapping and treats `bytes` fields as base64; the OTLP/JSON spec overrides this and encodes traceId/spanId as HEX. Every JSON ingest therefore base64-decodes a hex string, storing 24 bytes instead of 16, and still returns HTTP 200 {"partialSuccess":{}}. Add a normalizeOTLPJSONIDs pre-decode pass that rewrites traceId/spanId string fields from hex to the base64 protojson expects, keeping protojson as the single decoder so the spec deviation is confined to one function. Apply at otlp_receiver.go:166 (traces), otlp_receiver.go:233 (logs), and the metrics equivalent in otlp_receiver_metrics.go. Malformed IDs are REJECTED with a typed error and HTTP 400 per Design Freeze - no silent repair, no best-effort store. The protobuf path (otlp_receiver.go:161) is already correct and must not regress. ALSO in this milestone (code only, DISABLED by default): the shared-secret auth middleware on the three OTLP routes, gated on AILANG_OTLP_INGEST_TOKEN, using constantTimeEqual; unset env = auth off so the deploy cannot break live ingest.
acceptance_criteria: NON-VACUITY PROOF: the red-first transcript (--- FAIL showing a 48-char stored trace_id) is captured BEFORE internal/observatory/otlp_receiver.go is modified, and recorded verbatim in the commit body and this JSON's notes. Do NOT use git stash or git checkout to produce it (CLAUDE.md Principle 0)
An httptest POST of an OTLP/JSON body with traceId="5b8aa5a2d2c872e8321cf37308d69df2" through handleTraces stores exactly those 16 bytes; the test asserts the stored hex is 32 chars, not 24 or 48
A payload with traceId="not-hex" returns HTTP 400 with a typed error AND writes no row - asserted by a span count taken before and after, not by the status code alone
JSON and protobuf ingest of the same logical payload produce IDENTICAL stored trace_id and span_id. This is the cross-encoding invariant the bug violated
Codec unit tests cover: valid 16-byte trace ID, valid 8-byte span ID, wrong length, non-hex characters, empty string, and a value that is BOTH valid hex AND valid base64 (pins the precedence rule)
The protobuf path is provably unchanged: existing convertSpan tests green, plus a protobuf round-trip test asserting the same 16 bytes

Auth middleware tests: AILANG_OTLP_INGEST_TOKEN set + no header -> 401; set + wrong header -> 401; set + correct header -> 200; UNSET + no header -> 200 (the local-dev and current-prod path, which must keep working)

Auth is scoped to /v1/traces, /v1/logs, /v1/metrics ONLY - the dashboard UI and /api/observatory/* reads are untouched, asserted by a request to /api/observatory/spans succeeding with no header while the token is set

features.description: Repair the existing corrupted rows via a new internal/observatory/migrate_v18.go (v18 verified unallocated 2026-08-13; migrate_v16.go and migrate_v17.go are the current max). For every row whose trace_id is 48 hex chars, set trace_id = base64encode(unhexlify(trace_id)); same for span_id. The transform is lossless because base64 decoding is injective at fixed length - verified against live prod rows, e.g. 6bb6b86b6d3ad37e1bd9fe1f6b5736ebd6b9f766f8e1a6bd recovers to a7a4a206034b2f4fa1c269a592b44aa9. Guard strictly on length so the migration is idempotent and cannot touch already-correct 32-char rows.
acceptance_criteria: A row seeded with a known corrupted ID recovers the EXACT original hex - asserted against the measured live pair (6bb6b86b6d3ad37e1bd9fe1f6b5736ebd6b9f766f8e1a6bd -> a7a4a206034b2f4fa1c269a592b44aa9)
IDEMPOTENCE: running the migration twice produces a byte-identical DB, asserted by a checksum of the spans table, not by inspection
Rows with already-correct 32-char IDs are provably untouched: the count of modified rows equals the count of 48-char rows, asserted explicitly
The migration reports the number of rows repaired; a run against a DB with zero corrupted rows is a no-op that says so rather than failing
Span COUNT is unchanged before and after - this is a repair, never a delete

features.notes: Landed 281a8ebb2. Anchored to the production pair 6bb6b86b...a6bd -> a7a4a206034b2f4fa1c269a592b44aa9. Covers id/trace_id/parent_span_id. A test found a REAL defect: repairing a span id can collide with an existing row (same span ingested under both encodings), which violated the PK and rolled back the whole transaction; now skipped and reported loudly rather than deleted. Idempotence asserted by sha256 of the spans table; never-delete by row count. Also added CurrentSchemaVersion so a migration bump stops reddening unrelated tests. 7 new tests. | POST-DEPLOY CORRECTION 2026-08-13: this migration CANNOT repair the deployed environments. Both ailang-dashboard (prod) and ailang-dev-dashboard run AILANG_STORAGE=gcp, which selects fsstore.NewObservatoryStore (Firestore); MigrateWithVersion is only reachable from the two SQLite paths (observatory/store.go:61, backend_sqlite.go:32) and Firestore has no migration hook. The design doc assumed SQLite and never verified it - the V13 row counted prod rows but not which backend held them. The repair FUNCTION is correct and tested; it needs a Firestore-side runner. migrate_v18 still correctly repairs local/rig SQLite observatories.

features.description: Add the three OpenRouter Broadcast correlation fields - user (<=128 chars), session_id (<=256 chars), and trace (arbitrary key-value object) - so broadcast spans can be joined to eval runs. Add User/SessionID/Trace to chatRequest (internal/ai/openrouter/types.go:16-31) with omitempty, and the same to ai.Request (internal/ai/provider.go:32). Wire ALL THREE OpenRouter request-build sites: chat.go:44 (struct literal), step.go:187 (REUSE the existing marshalStepBodyWithExtras splice helper at step.go:186 - do not add a second body-extension mechanism), and streamstep.go:118. Populate from internal/eval_harness/ai_provider.go:81 using the chain ID as session_id. Enforce the length caps at construction, failing loudly with a typed error rather than silently truncating (CLAUDE.md Principle 2). Fully independent of M1/M2.
